draft.title: Photons
card: A photon is a single packet of light energy. Light is emitted and absorbed in these packets, not in a smooth, continuous flow.
The energy of one photon is E = hf. E is energy in joules, f is frequency in hertz, and h is Planck's constant, about 6.63 × 10^-34 J s.
Energy is directly proportional to frequency. Doubling the frequency doubles the energy of each photon.
Violet light has a higher frequency than red light, so each violet photon carries more energy than each red photon. Brightness is a different thing: it depends on how many photons arrive each second.
draft.remember: Each photon carries E = hf, so higher frequency means more energy per photon.

a.q: Which change would increase the energy carried by each photon of a light beam?
opts: Increasing the frequency of the light
Increasing the number of photons each second
Increasing the width of the beam
Increasing the time the light is switched on
a.why: E = hf, so the energy of one photon depends only on frequency. Sending more photons each second makes the beam brighter, but each photon still carries the same energy.
a.clue: Look at what the symbols in E = hf stand for.

b.q: Mia compares a dim violet laser with a bright red laser. Which statement about a single photon from each is correct?
opts: A violet photon has more energy than a red photon
A red photon has more energy because its beam is brighter
Both photons have equal energy because both are light
A red photon has more energy as its wavelength is longer
b.why: Violet light has a higher frequency than red light, so by E = hf each violet photon has more energy. Brightness depends on the number of photons each second, not the energy of one photon, so the bright red beam does not have more energetic photons.

a.best: Increasing the frequency of the light

b.best: A violet photon has more energy than a red photon
